title: Fieldbook: Seller Scenarios & Scripts v1
content:
Purpose:
A compact, scenario-driven slide set for sellers to run 10–20 minute qualification and technical-seller conversations. Focus is on rapid diagnosis, clear fallbacks, and pilot success criteria so SEs and AEs can convert trial/proof-of-value conversations into committed pilots with predictable scope and SLAs.

How to use this fieldbook (speaker notes):
- 5–10 minute quick-scan: use the Qualify Frame (slide 2) to identify the customer’s dominant constraint (latency, cost, data residency, or throughput).
- 10–20 minute technical follow-up: hand to an SE with the Scenario Script that matches the dominant constraint.
- If in doubt: run the "latency-cost taste test" (slide 6) to quickly reveal whether routing/pinning or quantization will be the most impactful lever.

Slide 1 — One-liner and agenda:
- One-liner: "Help engineering teams get predictable, low-latency LLM inference without building/owning the serving stack."
- Agenda bullets: Qualify -> Scenario script -> Evidence & pricing -> Pilot success metrics -> Hand-off checklist

Slide 2 — The Qualify Frame (3 diagnostic questions):
1) Usage pattern: bursty vs steady? (bursty -> routing/region fallback; steady -> reserved capacity)
2) Latency sensitivity: <200ms p50 vs okay with 500–800ms
3) Data controls: need VPC/HSM/audit logs?
Notes: Ask Q1 first — it often determines whether Dedicated or Hosted will be recommended.

Slide 3 — Scenario A: Low-latency interactive UI (customer example: docs assistant)
- Primary asks: p50 latency <200ms; consistency across regions; high concurrency in peak windows.
- Seller script: lead with p50 SLA capability and routing policy: "We can pin you to a dedicated pool and route by region, and burst to shared pools if needed."
- Quick technical checks for SE: tokenization profile, expected context window, expected peak RPS, tolerance for quantization
- Fallback path: if strict latency but limited budget -> propose small dedicated pool + aggressive prefix caching + 8-bit quantization for non-critical models

Slide 4 — Scenario B: High-throughput batch embeddings (customer example: search index rebuild)
- Primary asks: throughput and cost per embedding; predictable unit economics
- Seller script: emphasize batching, autoscaling, and cost controls: "We can reserve capacity and schedule jobs into low-cost windows; our Optimize recommendations typically cut unit cost by 20–40% for heavy embedding workloads."
- SE checklist: dataset size, expected concurrency, which models are acceptable for quality, desired embedding dimensionality
- Pilot criteria: run 100k embeddings in staged run, measure cost per 1k and quality delta vs baseline

Slide 5 — Scenario C: Regulated patient data (customer example: healthcare triage)
- Primary asks: data residency, auditability, encryption keys, on-prem option
- Seller script: map compliance needs to Private deployment features: KMS integration, audit logs, and air-gapped options; request security questionnaire early
- SE checklist: required certifications, inbound/outbound network rules, retention policies, audit frequency
- Pilot criteria: complete security questionnaire, provision VPC control plane, execute a short penetration checklist within 2 weeks

Slide 6 — Latency-Cost Taste Test (rapid A/B heuristics):
- Step A: Measure 50 tokens end-to-end latency for a canonical prompt in both Hosted and a small Dedicated pool (if available).
- Step B: If Dedicated improves p50 by >25% at 20% extra cost, recommend Dedicated.
- Step C: If cost delta is large and latency improvement small, recommend caching + model quantization instead.
- Quick script: "Let's run a 1-hour smoke where we send 100 representative requests to both configs and compare p50 and cost"

Slide 7 — Evidence matrix (how to show wins):
- Metrics to capture: p50/p95, tokens per $1, cache hit rate, cold start time, model quality delta (BLEU/ROUGE or human rating), incident rate during pilot
- Suggested artifacts: latency heatmap screenshot, cost-savings simulation CSV, short recording of user flows with timestamps

Slide 8 — Objections & short responses (seller-ready lines):
- "We can build this ourselves": "Yes, but building a production-grade runtime with batching, KV caching, and routing takes months and ongoing ops cost — our customers save engineering cycles and reduce per-token costs immediately."
- "We need absolute control over keys": "We support customer-managed KMS/HSM and private deployments with audit logs and limited control-plane exposure."
- "Vendor lock-in": "We expose model versioning and compatible model fallbacks; customers can export prompts and configs and run on Dedicated or Private with consistent APIs."

Slide 9 — Price framing and pilot packs (quick options):
- Small pilot (2–4 weeks): free Hosted credits for 50k tokens + SE 4 hours/week, success = reproducible p50 improvement or cost estimate within 10%
- Pilot with Dedicated eval: 30-day reserved trial at discounted commit, includes routing policy tuning and 1 canary rollout
- Custom enterprise: negotiated commit + extended SLAs + onboarding package

Slide 10 — Hand-off checklist to SE (copyable):
- Customer brief (1–2 sentences)
- Dominant constraint selected: latency | throughput | cost | compliance
- Canonical prompt and test corpus link
- Target metrics and thresholds for pilot success
- Primary contacts (AE, SE, Infra lead) and expected timelines

Appendix A — Rapid diagnostics command list for SEs (notes to SE):
- Commands to measure: p50/p95 (client + server), cache hit ratio, KV-cache warmup behavior, model size & quantization impact on latency
- Quick config toggles to try: reduce batching window, enable prefix caching, switch to quantized variant, pin model to dedicated pool, enable regional routing

Appendix B — Example roleplay script (AE + SE, 7 min):
- AE: "We onboard many teams in 48–72 hours. Tell me how latency/cost/regs are showing up for you today."
- Customer: short answer (AE captures dominant constraint)
- SE: rapid probing using the scenario checklist -> proposes pilot pack or follow-up deep-dive

Next steps / backlog items for this deck:
- Convert to 10-slide canonical deck for SDRs with 30s soundbites (owner: Priya Rao)
- Build a one-click lab kit for the Latency-Cost Taste Test (owner: Ethan Cole)
- Add two customer case screenshots and anonymized metrics (owner: Marketing)

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally prescriptive and lightweight — goal is repeatable conversations that reduce back-and-forth and accelerate pilot conversions. Looking for feedback on missing scenario types and pilot thresholds.
